scope: All8evaluation native1024PNG images inspected individually; warmup excluded. SDXL-Turbo512contact sheet reviewed for qualitative composition/aesthetic comparison.
conclusion: Promising coherent photographic priest portraits at1024with reliable collars and no hats in this small set. Major concern is near-duplicate identity impression within every prompt pair and modest hot-calendar aesthetic. Neither broad diversity nor production quality is established.

pair_resemblance.observation: Nearly same receding hairline, brows, head shape and friendly smile; feels like two photographs of one person.
Nearly same close-cropped hairstyle, facial proportions, brows, mouth and skin rendering; slight pose change.
Very similar round head, receding buzzcut, eyes and broad smile; strongly one-person impression.
Same short gray beard, receding gray hair and facial shape; pose/gaze changes dominate.

diversity_limit: Across prompts there are four distinguishable appearance families; within-prompt randomness contributes less identity change than required. This is visual similarity, not identity-recognition testing. Hash uniqueness alone is insufficient.

aesthetics_vs_turbo512.observation: FLUX1024has more usable native detail, fuller head-and-shoulders framing and convincing black garments/clerical tabs. It looks like a formal parish staff photo series. Turbo512looks softer but somewhat more calendar/editorial and attractive, especially the dark-haired and gray-haired prompts. Both repeat facial templates within prompt pairs. This comparison is subjective and does not override user taste.
aesthetics_vs_turbo512.limitation: Turbocomparison here is based on contact-sheet inspection, not a new individual512quality audit. Same seed numbers across different architectures do not mean matched identity.

timing_notes: See timing-notes.json. Recorded generation omits CPU noise creation and is not measured CUDA/server performance.
